for the embedding closest to that point."},{"start":927.0,"end":928.2,"text":"At least, kind of."},{"start":928.48,"end":931.773,"text":"Despite this being a classic example for the model I'm playing with,"},{"start":931.773,"end":935.937,"text":"the true embedding of queen is actually a little farther off than this would suggest,"},{"start":935.937,"end":939.957,"text":"presumably because the way queen is used in training data is not merely a feminine"},{"start":939.957,"end":940.78,"text":"version of king."},{"start":941.62,"end":945.26,"text":"When I played around, family relations seemed to illustrate the idea much better."},{"start":946.34,"end":950.461,"text":"The point is, it looks like during training the model found it advantageous to"},{"start":950.461,"end":954.9,"text":"choose embeddings such that one direction in this space encodes gender information."},{"start":956.8,"end":960.0809999999999,"text":"Another example is that if you take the embedding of Italy,"},{"start":960.081,"end":964.753,"text":"and you subtract the embedding of Germany, and add that to the embedding of Hitler,"},{"start":964.753,"end":968.09,"text":"you get something very close to the embedding of Mussolini."},{"start":968.57,"end":973.431,"text":"It's as if the model learned to associate some directions with Italian-ness,"},{"start":973.431,"end":975.6700000000001,"text":"and others with WWII axis leaders."},{"start":976.47,"end":979.931,"text":"Maybe my favorite example in this vein is how in some models,"},{"start":979.931,"end":984.187,"text":"if you take the difference between Germany and Japan, and add it to sushi,"},{"start":984.187,"end":986.23,"text":"you end up very close to bratwurst."},{"start":987.35,"end":990.187,"text":"Also in playing this game of finding nearest neighbors,"},{"start":990.187,"end":993.85,"text":"I was very pleased to see how close cat was to both beast and monster."},{"start":994.69,"end":997.743,"text":"One bit of mathematical intuition that's helpful to have in mind,"},{"start":997.743,"end":1000.703,"text":"especially for the next chapter, is how the dot product of two"},{"start":1000.703,"end":1003.85,"text":"vectors can be thought of as a way to measure how well they align."},{"start":1004.87,"end":1007.693,"text":"Computationally, dot products involve multiplying all the"},{"start":1007.693,"end":1011.111,"text":"corresponding components and then adding the results, which is good,"},{"start":1011.111,"end":1014.33,"text":"since so much of our computation has to look like weighted sums."},{"start":1015.19,"end":1019.999,"text":"Geometrically, the dot product is positive when vectors point in similar directions,"},{"start":1019.999,"end":1023.606,"text":"it's zero if they're perpendicular, and it's negative whenever"},{"start":1023.606,"end":1025.61,"text":"they point in opposite directions."},{"start":1026.55,"end":1029.916,"text":"For example, let's say you were playing with this model,"},{"start":1029.916,"end":1034.906,"text":"and you hypothesize that the embedding of cats minus cat might represent a sort of"},{"start":1034.906,"end":1037.01,"text":"plurality direction in this space."},{"start":1037.43,"end":1040.57,"text":"To test this, I'm going to take this vector and compute its dot"},{"start":1040.57,"end":1043.461,"text":"product against the embeddings of certain singular nouns,"},{"start":1043.461,"end":1047.05,"text":"and compare it to the dot products with the corresponding plural nouns."},{"start":1047.27,"end":1050.219,"text":"If you play around with this, you'll notice that the plural ones"},{"start":1050.219,"end":1053.628,"text":"do indeed seem to consistently give higher values than the singular ones,"},{"start":1053.628,"end":1056.07,"text":"indicating that they align more with this direction."},{"start":1057.07,"end":1061.616,"text":"It's also fun how if you take this dot product with the embeddings of the words one,"},{"start":1061.616,"end":1064.43,"text":"two, three, and so on, they give increasing values,"},{"start":1064.43,"end":1069.03,"text":"so it's as if we can quantitatively measure how plural the model finds a given word."},{"start":1070.25,"end":1073.57,"text":"Again, the specifics for how words get embedded is learned using data."},{"start":1074.05,"end":1077.475,"text":"This embedding matrix, whose columns tell us what happens to each word,"},{"start":1077.475,"end":1079.55,"text":"is the first pile of weights in our model."},{"start":1080.03,"end":1084.7269999999999,"text":"Using the GPT-3 numbers, the vocabulary size specifically is 50,257,"},{"start":1084.727,"end":1089.77,"text":"and again, technically this consists not of words per se, but of tokens."},{"start":1090.63,"end":1094.309,"text":"The embedding dimension is 12,288, and multiplying those"},{"start":1094.309,"end":1097.79,"text":"tells us this consists of about 617 million weights."},{"start":1098.25,"end":1100.626,"text":"Let's go ahead and add this to a running tally,"},{"start":1100.626,"end":1103.81,"text":"remembering that by the end we should count up to 175 billion."},{"start":1105.43,"end":1108.756,"text":"In the case of transformers, you really want to think of the vectors"},{"start":1108.756,"end":1112.13,"text":"in this embedding space as not merely representing individual words."},{"start":1112.55,"end":1116.513,"text":"For one thing, they also encode information about the position of that word,"},{"start":1116.513,"end":1119.224,"text":"which we'll talk about later, but more importantly,"},{"start":1119.224,"end":1122.77,"text":"you should think of them as having the capacity to soak in context."},{"start":1123.35,"end":1127.408,"text":"A vector that started its life as the embedding of the word king, for example,"},{"start":1127.408,"end":1131.413,"text":"might progressively get tugged and pulled by various blocks in this network,"},{"start":1131.413,"end":1135.575,"text":"so that by the end it points in a much more specific and nuanced direction that"},{"start":1135.575,"end":1138.592,"text":"somehow encodes that it was a king who lived in Scotland,"},{"start":1138.592,"end":1141.973,"text":"and who had achieved his post after murdering the previous king,"},{"start":1141.973,"end":1144.73,"text":"and who's being described in Shakespearean language."},{"start":1145.21,"end":1147.79,"text":"Think about your own understanding of a given word."},{"start":1148.25,"end":1151.727,"text":"The meaning of that word is clearly informed by the surroundings,"},{"start":1151.727,"end":1155.098,"text":"and sometimes this includes context from a long distance away,"},{"start":1155.098,"end":1159.645,"text":"so in putting together a model that has the ability to predict what word comes next,"},{"start":1159.645,"end":1163.3899999999999,"text":"the goal is to somehow empower it to incorporate context efficiently."},{"start":1164.05,"end":1167.136,"text":"To be clear, in that very first step, when you create the array of"},{"start":1167.136,"end":1170.363,"text":"vectors based on the input text, each one of those is simply plucked"},{"start":1170.363,"end":1173.496,"text":"out of the embedding matrix, so initially each one can only encode"},{"start":1173.496,"end":1176.77,"text":"the meaning of a single word without any input from its surroundings."},{"start":1177.71,"end":1181.562,"text":"But you should think of the primary goal of this network that it flows through"},{"start":1181.562,"end":1185.414,"text":"as being to enable each one of those vectors to soak up a meaning that's much"},{"start":1185.414,"end":1188.97,"text":"more rich and specific than what mere individual words could represent."},{"start":1189.51,"end":1192.802,"text":"The network can only process a fixed number of vectors at a time,"},{"start":1192.802,"end":1194.1699999999998,"text":"known as its context size."},{"start":1194.51,"end":1197.672,"text":"For GPT-3 it was trained with a context size of 2048,"},{"start":1197.672,"end":1202.803,"text":"so the data flowing through the network always looks like this array of 2048 columns,"},{"start":1202.803,"end":1205.0100000000002,"text":"each of which has 12,000 dimensions."},{"start":1205.59,"end":1208.657,"text":"This context size limits how much text the transformer can"},{"start":1208.657,"end":1211.83,"text":"incorporate when it's making a prediction of the next word."},{"start":1212.37,"end":1215.042,"text":"This is why long conversations with certain chatbots,"},{"start":1215.042,"end":1218.168,"text":"like the early versions of ChatGPT, often gave the feeling of"},{"start":1218.168,"end":1222.05,"text":"the bot kind of losing the thread of conversation as you continued too long."},{"start":1223.03,"end":1225.23,"text":"We'll go into the details of attention in due time,"},{"start":1225.23,"end":1228.81,"text":"but skipping ahead I want to talk for a minute about what happens at the very end."},{"start":1229.45,"end":1231.991,"text":"Remember, the desired output is a probability"},{"start":1231.991,"end":1234.87,"text":"distribution over all tokens that might come next."},{"start":1235.17,"end":1237.759,"text":"For example, if the very last word is Professor,"},{"start":1237.759,"end":1240.456,"text":"and the context includes words like Harry Potter,"},{"start":1240.456,"end":1243.531,"text":"and immediately preceding we see least favorite teacher,"},{"start":1243.531,"end":1247.685,"text":"and also if you give me some leeway by letting me pretend that tokens simply"},{"start":1247.685,"end":1251.892,"text":"look like full words, then a well-trained network that had built up knowledge"},{"start":1251.892,"end":1255.8300000000002,"text":"of Harry Potter would presumably assign a high number to the word Snape."},{"start":1256.51,"end":1257.97,"text":"This involves two different steps."},{"start":1258.31,"end":1263.052,"text":"The first one is to use another matrix that maps the very last vector in that"},{"start":1263.052,"end":1267.61,"text":"context to a list of 50,000 values, one for each token in the vocabulary."},{"start":1268.17,"end":1272.173,"text":"Then there's a function that normalizes this into a probability distribution,"},{"start":1272.173,"end":1275.657,"text":"it's called softmax and we'll talk more about it in just a second,"},{"start":1275.657,"end":1279.868,"text":"but before that it might seem a little bit weird to only use this last embedding"},{"start":1279.868,"end":1283.923,"text":"to make a prediction, when after all in that last step there are thousands of"},{"start":1283.923,"end":1288.29,"text":"other vectors in the layer just sitting there with their own context-rich meanings."},{"start":1288.93,"end":1292.677,"text":"This has to do with the fact that in the training process it turns out to be"},{"start":1292.677,"end":1296.424,"text":"much more efficient if you use each one of those vectors in the final layer"},{"start":1296.424,"end":1300.27,"text":"to simultaneously make a prediction for what would come immediately after it."},{"start":1300.97,"end":1303.24,"text":"There's a lot more to be said about training later on,"},{"start":1303.24,"end":1305.09,"text":"but I just want to call that out right now."},{"start":1305.73,"end":1309.69,"text":"This matrix is called the Unembedding matrix and we give it the label WU."},{"start":1310.21,"end":1313.574,"text":"Again, like all the weight matrices we see, its entries begin at random,"},{"start":1313.574,"end":1315.91,"text":"but they are learned during the training process."},{"start":1316.47,"end":1319.447,"text":"Keeping score on our total parameter count, this Unembedding"},{"start":1319.447,"end":1322.0279999999998,"text":"matrix has one row for each word in the vocabulary,"},{"start":1322.028,"end":1325.65,"text":"and each row has the same number of elements as the embedding dimension."},{"start":1326.41,"end":1330.381,"text":"It's very similar to the embedding matrix, just with the order swapped,"},{"start":1330.381,"end":1333.625,"text":"so it adds another 617 million parameters to the network,"},{"start":1333.625,"end":1336.589,"text":"meaning our count so far is a little over a billion,"},{"start":1336.589,"end":1340.224,"text":"a small but not wholly insignificant fraction of the 175 billion"},{"start":1340.224,"end":1341.79,"text":"we'll end up with in total."},{"start":1342.55,"end":1344.657,"text":"As the very last mini-lesson for this chapter,"},{"start":1344.657,"end":1346.9009999999998,"text":"I want to talk more about this softmax function,"},{"start":1346.901,"end":1350.6100000000001,"text":"since it makes another appearance for us once we dive into the attention blocks."},{"start":1351.43,"end":1356.554,"text":"The idea is that if you want a sequence of numbers to act as a probability distribution,"},{"start":1356.554,"end":1359.408,"text":"say a distribution over all possible next words,"},{"start":1359.408,"end":1364.59,"text":"then each value has to be between 0 and 1, and you also need all of them to add up to 1."},{"start":1365.25,"end":1369.892,"text":"However, if you're playing the deep learning game where everything you do looks like"},{"start":1369.892,"end":1374.81,"text":"matrix-vector multiplication, the outputs you get by default don't abide by this at all."},{"start":1375.33,"end":1377.7849999999999,"text":"The values are often negative, or much bigger than 1,"},{"start":1377.785,"end":1379.8700000000001,"text":"and they almost certainly don't add up to 1."},{"start":1380.51,"end":1384.03,"text":"Softmax is the standard way to turn an arbitrary list of numbers"},{"start":1384.03,"end":1388.705,"text":"into a valid distribution in such a way that the largest values end up closest to 1,"},{"start":1388.705,"end":1391.29,"text":"and the smaller values end up very close to 0."},{"start":1391.83,"end":1393.07,"text":"That's all you really need to know."},{"start":1393.09,"end":1397.129,"text":"But if you're curious, the way it works is to first raise e to the power"},{"start":1397.129,"end":1401.3919999999998,"text":"of each of the numbers, which means you now have a list of positive values,"},{"start":1401.392,"end":1405.599,"text":"and then you can take the sum of all those positive values and divide each"},{"start":1405.599,"end":1409.47,"text":"term by that sum, which normalizes it into a list that adds up to 1."},{"start":1410.17,"end":1414.286,"text":"You'll notice that if one of the numbers in the input is meaningfully bigger than the"},{"start":1414.286,"end":1417.966,"text":"rest, then in the output the corresponding term dominates the distribution,"},{"start":1417.966,"end":1422.1309999999999,"text":"so if you were sampling from it you'd almost certainly just be picking the maximizing"},{"start":1422.131,"end":1422.47,"text":"input."},{"start":1422.99,"end":1426.998,"text":"But it's softer than just picking the max in the sense that when other values"},{"start":1426.998,"end":1430.85,"text":"are similarly large, they also get meaningful weight in the distribution,"},{"start":1430.85,"end":1434.6499999999999,"text":"and everything changes continuously as you continuously vary the inputs."},{"start":1435.13,"end":1439.984,"text":"In some situations, like when ChatGPT is using this distribution to create a next word,"},{"start":1439.984,"end":1444.6699999999998,"text":"there's room for a little bit of extra fun by adding a little extra spice into this"},{"start":1444.67,"end":1448.91,"text":"function, with a constant T thrown into the denominator of those exponents."},{"start":1449.55,"end":1454.0,"text":"We call it the temperature, since it vaguely resembles the role of temperature in"},{"start":1454.0,"end":1458.121,"text":"certain thermodynamics equations, and the effect is that when T is larger,"},{"start":1458.121,"end":1462.681,"text":"you give more weight to the lower values, meaning the distribution is a little bit"},{"start":1462.681,"end":1466.911,"text":"more uniform, and if T is smaller, then the bigger values will dominate more"},{"start":1466.911,"end":1471.526,"text":"aggressively, where in the extreme, setting T equal to zero means all of the weight"},{"start":1471.526,"end":1472.79,"text":"goes to maximum value."},{"start":1473.47,"end":1477.662,"text":"For example, I'll have GPT-3 generate a story with the seed text,"},{"start":1477.662,"end":1482.95,"text":"\"once upon a time there was A\", but I'll use different temperatures in each case."},{"start":1483.63,"end":1488.283,"text":"Temperature zero means that it always goes with the most predictable word,"},{"start":1488.283,"end":1492.37,"text":"and what you get ends up being a trite derivative of Goldilocks."},{"start":1493.01,"end":1496.54,"text":"A higher temperature gives it a chance to choose less likely words,"},{"start":1496.54,"end":1497.9099999999999,"text":"but it comes with a risk."},{"start":1498.23,"end":1501.148,"text":"In this case, the story starts out more originally,"},{"start":1501.148,"end":1506.01,"text":"about a young web artist from South Korea, but it quickly degenerates into nonsense."},{"start":1506.95,"end":1510.8300000000002,"text":"Technically speaking, the API doesn't actually let you pick a temperature bigger than 2."},{"start":1511.17,"end":1515.336,"text":"There's no mathematical reason for this, it's just an arbitrary constraint imposed"},{"start":1515.336,"end":1519.35,"text":"to keep their tool from being seen generating things that are too nonsensical."},{"start":1519.87,"end":1524.272,"text":"So if you're curious, the way this animation is actually working is I'm taking the"},{"start":1524.272,"end":1527.011,"text":"20 most probable next tokens that GPT-3 generates,"},{"start":1527.011,"end":1529.5339999999999,"text":"which seems to be the maximum they'll give me,"},{"start":1529.534,"end":1532.97,"text":"and then I tweak the probabilities based on an exponent of 1/5."},{"start":1533.13,"end":1537.434,"text":"As another bit of jargon, in the same way that you might call the components of"},{"start":1537.434,"end":1542.173,"text":"the output of this function probabilities, people often refer to the inputs as logits,"},{"start":1542.173,"end":1546.15,"text":"or some people say logits, some people say logits, I'm gonna say logits."},{"start":1546.53,"end":1550.417,"text":"So for instance, when you feed in some text, you have all these word embeddings"},{"start":1550.417,"end":1553.9599999999998,"text":"flow through the network, and you do this final multiplication with the"},{"start":1553.96,"end":1558.241,"text":"unembedding matrix, machine learning people would refer to the components in that raw,"},{"start":1558.241,"end":1561.3899999999999,"text":"unnormalized output as the logits for the next word prediction."},{"start":1563.33,"end":1566.697,"text":"A lot of the goal with this chapter was to lay the foundations for"},{"start":1566.697,"end":1570.37,"text":"understanding the attention mechanism, Karate Kid wax-on-wax-off style."},{"start":1570.85,"end":1574.8899999999999,"text":"You see, if you have a strong intuition for word embeddings, for softmax,"},{"start":1574.89,"end":1579.206,"text":"for how dot products measure similarity, and also the underlying premise that"},{"start":1579.206,"end":1583.577,"text":"most of the calculations have to look like matrix multiplication with matrices"},{"start":1583.577,"end":1587.562,"text":"full of tunable parameters, then understanding the attention mechanism,"},{"start":1587.562,"end":1592.2099999999998,"text":"this cornerstone piece in the whole modern boom in AI, should be relatively smooth."},{"start":1592.65,"end":1594.51,"text":"For that, come join me in the next chapter."},{"start":1596.39,"end":1598.922,"text":"As I'm publishing this, a draft of that next chapter"},{"start":1598.922,"end":1601.21,"text":"is available for review by Patreon supporters."},{"start":1601.77,"end":1604.239,"text":"A final version should be up in public in a week or two,"},{"start":1604.239,"end":1607.3700000000001,"text":"it usually depends on how much I end up changing based on that review."},{"start":1607.81,"end":1609.7079999999999,"text":"In the meantime, if you want to dive into attention,"},{"start":1609.708,"end":1612.41,"text":"and if you want to help the channel out a little bit, it's there waiting."}]}
